sub_problem: hybrid fixed-step symplectic and barnes-hut strategy for minimal gravity simulation
associations: Symplectic stepping reduces secular drift in low-dimensional orbital tests.
Barnes-Hut approximation provides dominant throughput gains at N>=512.
Approximation error from high theta can suppress stability gains if close encounters dominate.
anomaly_results: random_n64 in symplectic_eval shows worse drift than baseline under current parameterization, indicating scenario-sensitive stability behavior.
Barnes-Hut speedups remain large while error increases with theta, motivating coupled theta-dt sweeps.

steering_directions.direction: Introduce hybrid symplectic+Barnes-Hut method for high-N runs.
steering_directions.rationale: Combines stability-oriented integration with proven scalability gains.
steering_directions.first_step: Implement symplectic kick-drift-kick using Barnes-Hut accelerations with theta=0.8.
steering_directions.expected_signal: At N=512, throughput remains >4x baseline while max energy drift falls vs Euler+Barnes-Hut.

validation_checks: Compare hybrid against baseline, symplectic-direct, and Euler-Barnes-Hut on identical seeds.
Track max energy drift, runtime/step, and final-position error against direct baseline.
Verify deterministic replay under seed=42 with canonical JSON outputs.
